Method of Attack: Backdoor and remote access Trojan (RAT) combo to take control of infected computers
Dropped via malspam emails linking to malicious files

BalkanDoor: command line control, creating remote shells, taking screenshots, unlocking victim's screen without password, downloading more payloads, persistence via malicious scripts adding Registry keys and Startup entries, connects to hardcoded C2 servers

BalkanRAT: drops legitimate Remote Utilities software for remote control, hides processes and firewall exceptions, injects userland rootkit, uses legitimate Remote Utilities infrastructure (rutils.com, server.rutils.com) for communication, hides presence of related processes, can unlock screen remotely
Impacted Systems: Computers of financial departments of organizations in Croatia, Serbia, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina
Attack Vector: Malspam emails with tax document attachments and decoy PDFs
Indicators of Compromise: C2 server domains (hardcoded list, including server.rutils.com, rutils.com)
SHA-1 hashes of BalkanDoor and BalkanRAT malware samples
Use of SCardListReadersA and SCardConnectA API functions to list smart cards
